headlines.article_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 1:25 01:25 Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving Squawk on the Street Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. Read more CNBC news on Nvidia Nvidia live updates: CEO Jensen Huang resigns, Colette Kress named interim chief Nvidia stock falls 10% as CEO Jensen Huang announces resignation PRO: How far could Nvidia's stock fall on Huang's resignation? What investors need to know Elon Musk says it would be an ‘honor’ to hire Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Is Nvidia too big to fail? Its AI financing web raises the stakes : Analysis 2 Min Ago Analysts race to downgrade Nvidia Analysts are growing bearish on Nvidia after an espionage scandal led to the exit of the company's CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. Several shops on the Street downgraded the artificial intelligence infrastructure stock, citing the leadership questions that are swirling around Nvidia in the wake of the scandal. "We find it hard to advocate stepping in here in size as there will no doubt be more allegations to come (there is a trope that says if you find two ants in your kitchen the best estimate of the total number of ants in your kitchen is not two...), both from internal issues as well as headlines related to the business, new governmental investigations etc.," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said Thursday in a note to clients. Keybanc analyst John Vinh echoed that sentiment in his own note to clients. "We believe Huang's departure represents a material increase in strategic, organizational, and execution risk that warrants a higher risk premium and lower valuation multiple for the stock," Vinh wrote. "While we expect core fundamentals to remain strong for the foreseeable future, we believe it will be challenging for NVDA to find a successor with the same leadership and strategic vision as Huang." ‘A dark day for Nvidia’: Here’s what analysts have been saying about Jensen Huang’s departure — Liz Napolitano 3 Min Ago Huang and Nvidia's close relationship with D.C. expected to change U.S. President Donald Trump (R) greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as Trump and AI executives hold a media briefing following a meeting on artificial intelligence outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images Huang had emerged as one of President Trump's closest allies in the AI build-out. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C., was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. — Kif Leswing 7 Min Ago Kress to gather Nvidia leadership today at company HQ Interim CEO Colette Kress will gather the company's executive team today at the chipmaker's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif., a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. Kress will discuss leadership and continuity plans with the group of high-level executives, according to the source, who asked not to be named because the details are confidential. — Seema Mody, Annie Palmer 13 Min Ago Huang to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving, Mast says Nvidia President and CEO Jensen Huang speaks to the media as he arrives for a meeting with the Senate Banking Committee on Capitol Hill on December 3, 2025 in Washington, DC. Anna Moneymaker | Getty Images House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla. told reporters on Thursday that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving. "He has agreed to come," Mast said. "We're in negotiations for which day." The hearing will likely be under oath and transcribed, with multiple committees involved. Mast said he told Huang that he would "subpoena him" if necessary. Mast said Congress isn't ruling out "public hearings for other people or other things down road." — Samantha Subin 19 Min Ago Retail traders buy the Nvidia dip Retail traders rushed in to buy Nvidia shares following Jensen Huang's resignation, with the stock drawing the biggest opening bid from individual traders ever recorded by Vanda Research. In the first 30 minutes of the regular session, retail traders bought a net $111 million of Nvidia shares, more than 40x a normal open. The buying on Thursday follows multiple days of strong retail demand for the chipmaker's stock. It was the most heavily bought security across Vanda's universe Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday this week, commanding multiple times more net buying than the next most-bought security. NVDA has accounted for 61% of all retail net buying this week. Demand has also spilled over into leveraged products: Retail investors put $42.5 million into six 2x long Nvidia ETFs from Monday through Wednesday, one of the largest three-day inflows on record, Vanda said. — Nick Wells 21 Min Ago Nvidia board hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang's affair watch now VIDEO 4:18 04:18 Pres. Disney's 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary as part of multiyear film deal
headlines.summary: Cosm has secured a new studio partnership with Disney that will bring "Star Wars: A New Hope" to its domes as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration.
headlines.article_text: 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with "Star Wars: A New Hope" early next year. This is Cosm's third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros. — and sixth theatrical release. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for a unique presentation of the film. In this article DIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A poster for Disney and Lucasfilm's "Star Wars: A New Hope" in shared reality at Cosm. Cosm The Force is strong with Cosm. On Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology company announced a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Company that will bring the original "Star Wars" to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Cosm's massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film's 50th anniversary in May. "We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties." This will be Cosm's sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros. to bring "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. The company is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal's "Shrek" in December. Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width fills much of the viewers' periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment. Cosm's LA venue playing "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" in shared reality. Courtesy of Cosm In this case, "Star Wars" will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they're traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film. "We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader's breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have," Scalice said. "And it's one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn't really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner." The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd's pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans. Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies. "What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom," Scalice said. "It's the No. 1 foundation for our business." And Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise launches, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands. headlines.article_text: Nebius Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nebius' earnings report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week. The companies' stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout. Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. In this article NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Arkady Volozh, CEO of Nebius and then Yandex CEO, speaks at the Artificial Intelligence Journey event in Moscow on Nov. 9, 2019. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: Loss of 13 cents per share Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts. Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart. Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%. Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report. Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing. The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress. Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 8 a.m. ET.
